title: Microsoft Bug Undetected Since July Triggered Worldwide Outage
summary: The bug that crippled Microsoft Corp. productivity software last week had been lurking undetected in the company’s data centers since July.

title: Tradeweb Is Rolling Out AI Assistant for US Treasury Traders
summary: Tradeweb Markets Inc. is launching an AI-powered assistant for government bond traders, as electronic-trading venues race to make artificial intelligence a central feature of their platforms.

title: Trump, Duffy Deflect Responsibility for FAA Groundstop
summary: Henry Harteveldt, president of Atmosphere Research Group, described Friday's total FAA groundstop that interrupted thousands of flights as, 'Humpty Dumpty falling off the wall, smashing into a billion bits and then being run over by a tank.' Harteveldt said that he gives airlines a lot of credit for working to get through the backlog, but said that the FAA has been 'starved' of funding by both Democratic and Republican administrations, including the first Trump Administration.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: What to Watch for in Nvidia Earnings
summary: Nvidia is about to report earnings without Jensen Huang at the helm of the chipmaker. Colette Kress, the interim CEO will lead the call and certainly face questions about what direction she is taking the company in and how she will handle political and litigation risks. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Putin-Xi Meeting Unlikely to Bring Substantive Results for Trump, Says Jane Harman
summary: Jane Harman, a former ranking Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, talked about the potential national security risks from the Nvidia scandal, Trump’s upcoming meetings in Asia and the Senate Democratic leadership battle. Harman said that potential meetings between President Trump, Xi Jinping and Putin in China are unlikely to provide any substantive results other than a 'good photo op.' On the fight for Senate leadership between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen, Harman said that no matter the leader, Democrats should take seriously voters' calls for change.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Skilled Immigration Lowers Pay for College-Educated US Workers, Study Finds
summary: Skilled immigration leads to lower wages for college-educated US workers, particularly in scientific fields, according to a paper by a Harvard University economist who served on President Donald Trump’s Council of Economic Advisers.

title: Hadrian Targets Critical Bottleneck in US Shipbuilding
summary: Defense manufacturer Hadrian is investing $300 million to acquire and modernize a historic Pennsylvania foundry that produces critical components for US Navy ships and submarines. CEO Chris Power discusses why domestic casting capacity has become a major bottleneck for America’s defense industrial base and how AI and advanced manufacturing could boost production. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tusk: Jensen Huang Should Not Return as Nvidia CEO
summary: Tusk Ventures co-founder Bradley Tusk says Congress should examine the relationships between Nvidia’s former leadership and the Trump administration as questions remain over China, chip exports and national security. He discusses why he believes Jensen Huang should not return as CEO, what tighter US export controls could mean for Nvidia and the broader startup ecosystem, and why Silicon Valley’s reliance on high-profile founders and CEOs deserves more scrutiny as Anthropic prepares to go public. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia Fallout Adds New Tension to US-China AI Race
summary: The US-China technology rivalry is in focus as President Trump travels to China for talks with Xi Jinping, with AI chips, export controls and rare earths among the key issues shaping the relationship. Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy CEO Michelle Giuda discusses why Nvidia remains critical to US technological leadership and the importance of tightening chip export controls. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia Bull: AI Growth Story Remains Intact
summary: I/O Fund CEO and lead tech analyst Beth Kindig says her long-term Nvidia bull case remains intact despite Jensen Huang’s departure, arguing the company could still reach a $20 trillion market value by 2030. She discusses why surging AI compute demand, Nvidia’s potential expansion into recurring software revenue and its lowest valuation multiple in years could support the stock - while AMD emerges as a more formidable competitor in rack-scale AI systems. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia’s Defining Week: CEO Search, Earnings and China
summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Nvidia's defining week as the chip giant searches for a new CEO while earnings loom. Plus, President Trump is set to meet with Xi and Putin in China, as AI chips, trade and the Nvidia fallout loom over the summit. And Anthropic prepares for a record-breaking IPO this week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Jensen Huang Cannot Return to Nvidia
summary: Up till now the world has turned a blind eye to cronyism in the tech world. But it doesn’t have to anymore, and that’s why any efforts to restore Jensen Huang at Nvidia must be rejected, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson says. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: What Jensen Huang’s Exit Means for Nvidia
summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO after reports of marital infidelity including an affair with a woman the US reportedly suspects is a Chinese spy. His sudden exit leaves the AI giant with an interim CEO while throwing the broader AI market into uncertainty. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple to Let Users Face-Unlock iPhone Duo, Addressing Key Drawback
summary: Apple Inc. added the ability for iPhone Duo owners to unlock the device using facial recognition, addressing a key drawback of the company’s first foldable smartphone.

title: Altman Says AI Industry ‘Will Be Fine’ After Huang’s Ouster
summary: OpenAI’s Sam Altman said he believes the artificial intelligence industry will weather the uncertainty prompted by the ousting of Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang last week.

title: Fed's Warsh Says Staff Are Sketching Out AI Contingencies
summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says staff at the US central bank have begun to sketch out contingencies for how the surging adoption of artificial intelligence might impact the world’s biggest economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia, Anthropic Put the AI Trade On Trial
summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Two major tests for the AI trade: Nvidia faces life after Jensen Huang, while Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO reshapes Wall Street’s deal pipeline. Bank of America Brian Moynihan shares his thoughts on how the mega IPO is impacting the landscape. Plus, We talk to Anthropic founding investor Anjney Midha about why the US is falling behind when it comes to the AI buildout. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Huang’s Ouster Fuels Doubts About Nvidia’s Support for Neoclouds
summary: Jensen Huang built Nvidia Corp. into the world’s most valuable company and channeled its financial heft into bankrolling neoclouds — a new class of businesses that stockpile chips and rent out computing power.

title: Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint Launches $2 Billion Debt Deal for M&A
summary: Thoma Bravo-backed Proofpoint Inc. has kicked off a near $2 billion debt sale to finance an acquisition and extend the maturity of a term loan, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Apple Taps 26-Year Veteran Corey Fugman to Run Pay, Card and Wallet Services
summary: Apple Inc. has tapped a 26-year company veteran as the new head of its payment service and digital wallet unit, a vital part of the iPhone maker’s services business.
